extracted.intended_audience: compliance officers and regulatory affairs staff at financial institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting comment letters in response to regulatory proposals, focused on financial institutions seeking to influence rulemaking. Covers content, tone, process, and coordination considerations to maximize impact while protecting sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughly Review the Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Read it carefully and consult industry resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read the full proposal and relevant supporting materials before drafting comments. Consult industry resources and interpretive guidance to understand scope and implications for your institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer Agency Questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and respond to specific questions in the request for comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map your responses to each specific question posed by the agency; explicit answers are more useful to reviewers and more likely to influence changes than general commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stick to Facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid emotional language; provide factual support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Real insights that demonstrate the validity of your points. Agencies respond particularly well to data and examples." Use empirical data, concrete examples, citations, and documented impacts rather than opinion or rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific aspects of the regulatory proposal that you find concerning rather than expressing general dissatisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference precise provisions, sections, or proposed changes and explain the problem and its real-world consequence. Specificity helps agencies identify and address issues in the rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer Solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Move beyond complaints; suggest practical refinements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose clear, actionable alternatives or drafting edits the agency could adopt. Offering workable solutions increases the credibility and utility of your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather Internal Input
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit perspectives from relevant internal stakeholders (legal, operations, risk, product, compliance) to ensure comments reflect operational realities and cover technical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider Collaborative Efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with trade associations and peers when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with industry groups or peers to amplify shared concerns, align proposed fixes, and present unified data or positions where beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep It Concise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep letters focused on the most important issues; avoid long, unfocused narratives. Clear, succinct comments are more likely to be read and acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Counterarguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate opposing viewpoints and develop rebuttals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider likely agency rationales or other stakeholders' perspectives and proactively rebut them with facts, reasoning, or alternative proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect Sensitive Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments become public — avoid confidential details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include proprietary, confidential, or personally identifiable information in your submission. Redact or summarize sensitive material and rely on aggregate data when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the agency's filing window (commonly 30–60 days for financial rulemaking) and file on time; missing the deadline typically prevents consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: The letter represents your institution publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a professional tone and polished presentation; the comment is a public document that reflects on your institution's reputation. Avoid emotional language and ensure accuracy and civility.
